Support Boats — Back and Forth

By the time you read this, the racing season will be drawing to a close for most of us. Therefore rather than publish
the smallest of rosters I thought I would reflect on the season just gone and look towards next years sailing
calendar, which even now is being planned. Again, we managed a full racing programme with the cats and the
mono hull fleets, always being covered by adequate support on the water from the RIB and Jack B. No mean feat as
we continued to have some no shows but thankfully someone always seemed to volunteer, often foregoing sailing
themselves to ensure racing went ahead. I won’t name names but these heroes know who they are and I am grateful
to them, as I am sure are all those who race. I would though like to mention the cruiser fleet members who can
always be relied upon when it comes to crewing the Jack B.
The club has been very fortunate this year in that funds have been made available to pay for RYA powerboat
training to level 2 for interested members. So far we have put 6 people through the programme run at Bradwell, and
we are building a healthy core of RYA trained people who can drive the RIB. Hopefully we can continue this
through next year.
Looking to next year, again I plan to generally allocate 2 duties to those of you who have volunteered to help with
the support boats, although the newly trained RYA people can expect to be asked to do perhaps just one extra! The
programme will be published as soon as practical, but meanwhile I shall use the intervening months to publish, in
Navigans, the list of names and contact details of those that have volunteered to do support boat duties, please take
some time to check for your name and that the phone numbers are correct. Let me know of any errors.
Thanks for your help and have a happy off season.
Les Hurrell-Smith

Purchase of the Stansgate site, and all the churn which went with it, has been a huge distraction to your Executive
Committee this year. The task was rightly given top priority, and has resulted in a successful outcome. In my

COMPANIES ACT 1985 - 1989
COMPANY LIMITED BY GUARANTEE AND NOT HAVING A SHARE CAPITAL
MEMORANDUM OF ASSOCIATION
of
THIRSLET SAILING CLUB LIMITED
Name
The name of the company is Thirslet Sailing Club Limited.

Registered office
The registered office of the company will be situated in England.

Objects
The company’s objects are:
3.1 to acquire and take over all or any part of the assets and liabilities of the present unincorporated body known as MASC, Beehive Lane, Chelmsford
to promote sailing and to encourage social intercourse among the members of the company;
3.3 to establish, maintain and conduct a club for the accommodation of the members of the company and their friends, and generally to afford to them all the
usual privileges, advantages and accommodation of a club;
3.4 to acquire by purchase, lease, or otherwise grounds at Marconi Sailing Club, Stansgate Road, Steeple, Essex and to lay out, and maintain the same for the
sport of sailing and the benefit of its members and to build or otherwise provide a clubhouse and other usual facilities in connection with it, and to furnish,
modify and maintain it, and to permit it to be used by members their friends and employees of the company and others, either gratuitously or for payment;
3.5 to acquire by purchase, lease or otherwise any other lands or property contiguous or near to the premises of the company, and such as may be deemed by the
company likely to advance or benefit, either directly or indirectly, the interest of the company;
3.6 to manage, improve, cultivate and maintain all or any part of the lands and other property of the company, and to demise, sell or otherwise deal with and
dispose of them, either together or in portions, for such consideration as the company may think fit, and, in particular, for shares, debentures or securities of
any company purchasing them;
3.7 to purchase, hire, make or provide and maintain, and to sell or otherwise dispose of all kinds of equipment and other things required or which may be
conveniently used in connection with the grounds, clubhouse and other premises of the company by persons frequenting them, whether members of the
company or not;
3.8 to buy, prepare, make, supply sell and deal in all kinds of apparatus and equipment used in connection with sailing and in all kinds of liquors provisions and
refreshments required or used by the members of the company or other persons using the grounds, clubhouse or premises of the company;
3.9 to hire and employ all classes of persons considered necessary for the purposes of the company and to pay them and other persons in return for services
tendered to the company salaries, wages, charges and pensions;
3.10 to promote and hold, either alone or jointly with any other association, club or persons, meetings, competitions or races associated with the sport of sailing
or other athletic sports and to offer, give or contribute towards prizes medals and awards for the sport of sailing and to promote, give or support dinners,
balls, concerts and other entertainments;
3:11 to establish, promote or assist in establishing or promoting, and to subscribe to, or become a member of, any other associations or clubs whose objects are
similar or in part similar to the objects of the company, or the establishment or promotion of which may be beneficial to the company provided that no
subscription may be paid to any such other association or club out of the funds of the company, except bona fide in furtherance of the objects of the
company;

3:12 to support and subscribe to any charitable or public body and any institution, society or club that may be for the benefit of the company or its employees, or
may be connected with the sport of sailing; to give pensions, gratuities, Christmas boxes or charitable aid to any person who may have served the company,
or to the wife, widow, children or other relatives of any such person; to make payments towards insurance; and to form and contribute to provident and
benefit funds for the benefit of any persons employed by the company;
3:13 to invest and deal with the money of the company not immediately required upon such securities and in such manner as may from time to time be
determined;
3.14 to borrow or raise and give security for money by the issue of or upon bonds, debentures, debenture stock, bills of exchange, promissory notes or other
obligations or securities of the company or by mortgage or charge upon all or any part of the property of the company;
3.15 to do such things as the directors consider to be in the best interests of this club and
3.16 to do all such other lawful things as are incidental or conducive to the attainment of the above objects or any of them
3.17 To retain within the Company all profits and surpluses to maintain or improve the Company's facilities. No profit or surplus will be distributed other than
upon dissolution of the Company.

Limited Liability
The liability of the members is limited.

Undertaking to contribute to assets
Every member of the company undertakes to contribute such amount (not exceeding £1.00) to the company’s assets if it is wound up while he is a member
or within one year after he ceases to be a member as may be required for payment of the company’s debts and liabilities contracted before he ceases to be a

THIRSLET SAILING CLUB LIMITED

1. Interpretation
In these articles:
1.1 ‘the Act’ means the Companies Act 1985 including any statutory modification or re-enactment of it for the time being in force;
12 ‘the Club’ means Thirslet Sailing Club Limited;
1.3 ‘secretary’ means the company secretary of the club or any other person appointed to perform the duties of the secretary of the club, including a joint,
assistant or deputy secretary;
1.4 unless the context otherwise requires, words or expressions contained in these articles bear the same meaning as in the Act but excluding any statutory
modification not in force when these articles become binding on the club;
1.5 the masculine includes the feminine and, where appropriate, the singular the plural.

2. Objects
The club is established for the purposes expressed in the memorandum of association.

3: Membership
3.1 The number of members with which the club proposes to be registered is 500 (Five Hundred) but the directors may, whenever the business of the club
Requires it, authorise an increase of members. :
3.2 Everyone that has an interest in sailing yachts, dinghies and similar vessels propelled by sails along with their families is qualified to be elected a member of
the club.
3:3 The first members of the club are the signatories to the memorandum of association and these articles and every person who at the date of incorporation of
the club had paid an entrance fee to, and was a member of, the unincorporated club known as MASC, Beehive Lane, Chelmsford, Sailing Section referred to
in paragraph 3.1 of the memorandum of association, and who, on or before 31 December 2003, or during such extended period as the directors may
determine, signs and delivers to the secretary of the club the form of membership prescribed by the directors.

4. Proposal of members
4.1 Except as provided in articles 3.3 and 8 every candidate for membership of the club must be proposed by one member of the club and seconded by another
member of the club, to both of whom the candidate must be personally known, and who are to be responsible for his eligibility.
42 The application for membership of every candidate must be in writing, signed by the candidate and his proposer and seconder, and must be in the form that
the directors from time to time prescribe.

5; Subscriptions
The annual and other subscriptions and entrance fee (if any) payable by members of the club are to be such as the directors from time to time prescribe.
5.2 The directors may provide either generally or as respects any particular member or members for payment of annual subscriptions by instalments.
5:3 Every application for membership must be accompanied by a remittance to cover the entrance fee (if any) and the appropriate subscription from the date of
application to the following 31 December and in the event of non-election the remittance must be returned to the candidate.

6. Life members and Vice Presidents
6.1 On the recommendation of the directors any person being a member of the club may, at any general meeting of the club, be elected an honorary life member
of the club without any special payment for such life membership.
6.2 A two-thirds’ majority of those present and entitled to vote is necessary for election of an honorary life member.
6.3 Every honorary life member is entitled to all the privileges and subject to all the duties of a member of the club during his life (subject, nevertheless, to the
provisions of article 13) without any further payment of annual membership except in respect of Boat Permit, Winter Storage, and Mooring fees, and except
in respect of his guarantee contained in clause 5 of the memorandum of association of this club.
6.4 The total number of honorary life members shall not however at any one time exceed the greater of five per cent of the total number of members nor twenty
in number
6.5 On the recommendation of the directors any person being a member of the club may, at any general meeting of the club, be elected a vice president.
6.6 The total number of vice presidents shall not, however, at any one time, exceed ten in number.

7. Categories of Membership

The categories of membership of the club shall be full member, family member, junior member, honorary life member, senior life member, honorary affiliated member,
temporary member and student member and the rights attaching to each such category shall be subject to the express provisions of these articles and to the
memorandum of association, and to any byelaws made by the directors of the club as provided below for the time being in force.

8. Temporary and other members

The directors of the club may, upon such terms and subject to such regulations as they may from time to time deem advisable and subject to article 4, propose as
members of the club:
8.1 persons who are visiting or temporarily resident in the district of Essex (‘temporary members’);
8.2 visitors;
but there may not be more than 75 such members of the club at any one time.

9. Election of members
9.1 Every candidate for election (including candidates for election to the special classes of membership specified in article 8.1 and 8.2) must be balloted for by
the directors of the club and a majority will exclude.
92 The name, address and description of every candidate, and the names of his proposer and seconder must be sent to the secretary in writing, and these
particulars must be posted in a conspicuous place in the clubhouse of the club 14 days at least before the ballot
9.3 On the unanimous recommendation of the directors in meeting duly convened, the ballot may take place before the expiration of 14 days but not earlier than
two days after the application of the candidate is received and not without the application being posted in the clubhouse.

10. Rights of members
10.1 Subject to the express provisions of these articles and to the memorandum of association, and to any byelaws made by the directors of the club as provided
below for the time being in force, all members of the club are entitled at all times to use all the premises and property of the club in common, and to be
supplied, at such charges as the directors from time to time determine, with whatever meals, refreshments and things are provided by the club for the use of
its members.
10.2 Subject to the provisions of these articles every member is entitled to all the rights and subject to all the duties of a member of the club provided that
temporary, junior and honorary affiliated members and visitors do not have the right to nominate or be elected as officers or directors of the club.

11. Notice of resignation
Any member wishing to resign his membership of the club must give notice in writing of his intention to do so, addressed to the secretary and deposited at the 4
registered office of the club before 01 January in any year, failing which the member must pay the subscription for the next year.

12. Non-payment of subscriptions 7

12.1 Any member whose annual subscription is unpaid on 28 February in any year ceases to be a member of the club and forfeits all right in and claim upon the %
am

club and its property unless the directors suspend the operation of this provision, which they may do as regards any particular member on such terms as they
determine at their discretion.
12.2 Where the directors have resolved in accordance with article 5 that the subscription of any particular member may be paid by instalments, this article applies
to non-payment of any instalment, substituting the due date of the instalment for 28 February.
13. Expulsion of members
13.1 If the conduct of any member is in the opinion of the directors injurious to the character of the club or objectionable in any respect, that member may be
required by the directors to resign, and, if he does not resign within one week, the member may (after he has been given the opportunity to justify or explain
his conduct) be expelled by resolution of the directors and then ceases to be a member of the club, and all sums that have been paid by the member are
forfeited.
13.2 A member expelled under this article may appeal by giving written notice of appeal to the secretary within 10 days from the posting of the notice of
expulsion.
b3:3. Upon receipt of a notice of appeal an extraordinary meeting must be convened within 14 days and, if that meeting passes an extraordinary resolution
rescinding the expulsion, then the member must be reinstated as from the date of the resolution.
13.4 If any member is convicted on indictment of any criminal offence or is adjudged a bankrupt, or makes any composition or arrangement with his creditors or,
being engaged in any profession, is prohibited by the disciplinary body of that profession from continuing to practice that member ipso facto ceases to be a
member of the club but any person so ceasing to be a member may be readmitted to membership by the directors at their discretion.
13:5 Any member expelled in accordance with these articles, or otherwise ceasing to be a member of the club, forfeits all right to or claim upon the club or its
property or funds or any return of fees paid and remains liable for any outstanding fees or charges due from him at the date of expulsion or cessation.

14. Rights of members personal
The rights of a member as such are personal and are not transferable and cease upon his death.

15. Annual general meeting
15.1 The club must hold a general meeting in each year as its annual general meeting in addition to any other meetings in that year, and must specify the meeting
as the annual general meeting in the notices calling it.
15.2 Not more than fourteen months may elapse between the date of one annual general meeting of the company and that of the next.
15.3 The annual general meeting must be held at such time and place as the directors appoint.

16. Extraordinary general meetings

16.1 All general meetings other than annual general meetings must be called extra-ordinary general meetings.
16.2 The directors may, whenever they think fit, and must, on a requisition made in writing by at least thirty members or members representing not less than one-
tenth of the total voting rights of all the members having at the date of deposit of the requisition a right to vote at general meetings, whichever is the lesser,
convene an extraordinary general meeting.
16.3 Any requisition made by the members must state the object of the meeting proposed to be called, and must be signed by the requisitionists and deposited at
the registered office of the club.
16.4 On receipt of the requisition the directors must immediately proceed to convene an extraordinary general meeting.
16.5 If the directors do not proceed to call a meeting within 21 days from the date of deposit of the requisition, the requisitionists, or any of them representing
more than one-half of the total voting rights of all of them, may convene such a meeting.
16.6 The expenses of notification of and the holding of a meeting called as a result of a requisition shall be borne by the requisitionists who shall deposit with the
club a sum reasonably sufficient to meet the club’s expenses in relation thereto save that the club will refund to the requisitionists the amount of such
expenses in the event that any proposed resolution made known by the requisition is carried.

17. Notice of meetings
Accidental omission to give notice of any meeting to or non-receipt of such notice by any member does not invalidate the proceedings at that meeting.

18. Quorum
18.1 No business may be transacted at any meeting unless a quorum is present.
18.2 Save as otherwise provided in these articles, thirty members personally present is a quorum
18.3 If within half an hour from the time appointed for the meeting a quorum of members is not present, or, if during a meeting such a quorum ceases to be
present:
18.3.1 if the meeting was convened on the requisition of members, it must be dissolved;
18.3.2 in any other case the meeting stands adjourned to the same day in the next week at the same time and place or to such time and place as the
directors may determine and, if at the adjourned meeting a quorum of members is not present within half an hour of the time appointed for the
meeting, the members present may form a quorum.

19. Chairman
19.1 The commodore, and failing him the vice-commodore, must preside as chairman at every general meeting of the club.
19.2 If there is no such chairman, or, if at any meeting he is not present within 15 minutes of the time of holding the meeting, the members present may elect one
of their number who is a director to be chairman of the meeting.
19.3 If there is no director present, then the members may elect any one of their number to be chairman of the meeting.

20. Adjournment
20.1 The chairman may, with the consent of a meeting at which a quorum is present (and must if so directed by the meeting), adjourn the meeting from time to
time and from place to place.
20.2 No business may be transacted at any adjourned meeting other than business which might properly have been transacted at the meeting had the adjournment
not taken place.

21. Passing of resolutions
21) At any general meeting:
211 a declaration by the chairman that a resolution has been carried, or carried unanimously, or carried by a particular majority, or lost, or not carried
by a particular majority, and
21:12 an entry to that effect in the book of proceedings of the club
are conclusive evidence of the fact without proof of the number or proportion of the votes recorded in favour of or against the resolution, unless a poll is
demanded by the chairman or by at least two members having the right to vote at the meeting or by a member or members representing not less than one-
tenth of the total voting rights of all the members having the right to vote at the meeting.
21.2 If a poll is demanded in the above manner, it must be taken in such manner as the chairman directs, and the result of the poll is deemed to be the resolution
of the meeting at which the poll was demanded.

22. Voting rights

22.1 Every member of the club may attend general meetings of the club but only full members, family members, student members, senior life members and
honorary life members may vote at such meetings.

+ 22.2
22.3
No member may vote at any meeting unless all the money then due from him to the club has been paid.
Every member of the club entitled to vote has one vote (save in the case of family members where there shall be one vote per family unit exercisable by one
person over the age of 18) and no more, except that, in case of equality of votes, the chairman may have a second or casting vote.

23. Proxy voting
23.1 On a poll votes may be given either personally or by proxy.
23.2 A proxy must be appointed in writing under the hand of the appointor.
23.3 The instrument appointing a proxy must be deposited at the registered office of the club not less than 48 hours before the time of holding the meeting at
which the person named in such instrument proposes to vote.
23.4 Any instrument appointing a proxy must be in the following form:
THIRSLET SAILING CLUB LIMITED
[I or We], (name) of (address), being [a member or members] of the above named club, appoint (name) of (address), or, failing him, (name) of (address),
as [my or our] proxy to vote in [my or our] name [s] and on [my or our] behalf at the [annual or extraordinary] general meeting of the club to be held on
(date) and at any adjournment.
Dated:
(signature(s) of members(s))

24. Directors
24.1 The directors of the club are the commodore, two vice-commodores, two rear-commodores, honorary treasurer elected as provided in these articles.
24.2 Four directors are a quorum at a directors’ meeting.
24.3 The commodore, and failing him a vice-commodore, must preside as chairman who in case of equality of votes may have a casting vote.

25. Officers
25:1 The officers of the club are the president, vice-president(s), commodore, two vice-commodores, two rear-commodores, honorary treasurer and secretary, all
of whom must be members of the club.
25:2 The immediate past commodore is to be an ex officio officer of the club during the period of his immediate past captaincy.
25.3 The first officers of the club are :-
President: Tony Benn
Vice Presidents: Steve Glynn, Peter Clayton, Clive Shenton, Peter Bloomfield and Frank Bennett
Commodore: Neil Pembleton
Vice-Commodore: David Payne
Rear-Commodore: John Salmon
Hon. Treasurer: John Bird
Secretary: Patrick Black

26. Remuneration
No director or officer of the club, other than the secretary, may receive any remuneration for his services in the capacity of director or officer but nothing contained in
these articles is to prohibit payment by the club of any sum to the secretary for clerical or other assistance.

27. Age limits
There is not any age limit for directors and accordingly Section 293(2)-(6) of the Act does not apply to the Club.

28. Retirement of directors and officers
28.1 At every annual general meeting of the club, the officers and directors other than the secretary must retire from office.
28.2 The retiring officers and directors are eligible for re-election at the same or any other general meeting of the club.

29. Election of officers
Subject as provided above, the election of officers other than the secretary and other directors of the club, must take place in the following manner:
29.1 Any two members of the club may nominate any other member to serve as an officer or director of the club, having previously received his assent.
29.2 The name of each member so nominated, together with the names of his proposer and seconder, must be sent in writing signed by all three of them to the
secretary of the club at least 21 days before the annual general meeting.
29.3 A list of the candidates’ names in alphabetical order, with the proposers’ and seconders’ names, must be posted in a conspicuous place in the club-house of
the club at least 14 days immediately preceding the annual general meeting.
29.4 Balloting lists must be prepared (if necessary) containing the names of the candidates only in alphabetical order.
29.5 Each member present at the annual general meeting and qualified to vote may vote for any number of candidates not exceeding the number of vacancies.
29.6 If insufficient candidates are nominated, the directors may elect a member or members to fill the remaining vacancy or vacancies.
29.7 If any candidate declines to serve after being elected, the candidate who has the next largest number of votes must be deemed to be elected.
29.8 If two or more candidates obtain an equal number of votes, the directors must select by lot from such candidates the candidate or candidates who is or are to
be elected.

30. Appointment of secretary
30.1 The secretary of the club must be appointed by the directors for such term, at such remuneration and upon such conditions as they think fit.
30.2 The directors may terminate the secretary’s appointment and fill a vacancy in the office.

31. Casual vacancies
31.1 All casual vacancies arising amongst the directors or officers of the club must be filled by the directors.
312 Any director or any officer (other than the secretary) appointed to fill a casual vacancy must retire at the following annual general meeting.

32. Removal of directors
The office of a director is vacated if:
32.1 his membership of the club is terminated in accordance with article 13.4;
32.2 he absents himself from meetings of the directors for a continuous period of six calendar months without special leave of absence from the other directors;
or

32.3 he gives the directors one calendar month’s notice in writing that he resigns his office or
32.4 he is removed by extraordinary resolution passed at a general meeting of the club.

33. Accounts
33.1 The directors of the club must ensure that proper books of account are kept in respect of:
33.1.1 all sums of money received and expended by the club and the matters in respect of which the receipts and expenditure take place and
33.1:2 the assets and liabilities of the club.
33.2 The books of account must be kept at the registered office of the club, or at such other place or places as the directors think fit, and must always be open to
the inspection of the directors.
33.3 The directors must from time to time determine whether, and to what extent, and at what times and places, and under what conditions and regulations, the
accounts and books of the club, or any of them, are to be open to the inspection of members of the club who are not directors.

33.4 No member who is not a director has any right to inspect any account or book or document of the club except as conferred by statute or authorised by the
directors.

34, Presentation of accounts
34.1 Once at least in every year the directors must lay before the club in general meeting an account of income and expenditure for the period since the preceding
account.
34.2 A balance sheet must be made out in every year and laid before the club in general meeting, made up to a date not more than six months before such
meeting.
34.3 A copy of the balance sheet must be sent to, or made available to, the persons entitled to receive notices of general meetings in the manner in which notices
are to be given under these articles 21 days prior to the meeting.
34.4 Every account and balance sheet must be accompanied by a report of the directors and the account, report and balance sheet must be signed by two directors
and countersigned by the secretary.

35. Powers of directors
35.1 The directors of the club may exercise all powers that may be exercised by the club and do anything that may be done by the club, except where under these
articles or any statute for the time being in force the power must be exercised or the thing be done by the club in general meeting.
35.2 The directors may act notwithstanding vacancies.
35.3 The directors of the club may issue debentures, debenture stock, bonds, or obligations of the club at any time, in any form or manner, and for any amount,
and may raise or borrow for the purpose of the club any sum or sums of money either upon mortgage or charge of all or any of the property of the club,
whether present or future, or on bonds or debentures secured by trust deed or otherwise or not secured as they may think fit.

36. Byelaws
36.1 The directors of the club may from time to time make, alter and repeal any byelaws they consider necessary or expedient or convenient for the proper
conduct and management of the club, and in particular, but not exclusively, they may by such byelaws:
36.1.1 regulate the terms and conditions upon which different categories of members and their guests, as well as visitors, may use the premises and
property of the club;
36.1.2 fix the times of opening and closing clubhouse, and premises of the club or any part of them and the permitted hours for the supply of
intoxicating liquor;
36.1.3 promulgate the rules to be observed and the prizes or stakes to be played for by members of the club playing any games on the premises of the
club;
36.1.4 prohibit particular games on the premises of the club entirely or at any particular time or times;
36.1.5 regulate the conduct of members of the club in relation to one another and to the club’s staff;
36.1.6 set aside the whole or any part or parts of the club’s premises for gentlemen members, women members or any other class or classes of members,
at any particular time or times, or for any particular purpose or purposes;
36.1.7 impose fines for breach of any byelaw or any article of association of the club and
36.1.8 regulate all matters that are commonly the subject of club rules.
36.2 The directors must adopt whatever means they consider sufficient to bring all byelaws, alterations and repeals to the notice of the members of the club.
36.3 All byelaws, so long as they are in force, are binding on all members of the club.
36.4 No byelaws may be inconsistent with, or affect or repeal anything contained in, the memorandum or articles of association of the club, or be in breach of any
statutory provision.
36.5 Any byelaw may be set aside by a special resolution of a general meeting of the club.

37. Delegation
37:1 The directors of the club may delegate any of their powers to a committee or committees appointed by the directors.
37.2 With the exception of a sub-committee with less than four members or one concerned with the purchase for the club, or supply by the club, of intoxicating
liquor, a sub-committee shall be chaired by an officer or director.
37.3 In the exercise of the powers delegated to it, a committee must conform to any regulations prescribed by the directors.
37.4 Any delegation of powers or appointment of a committee may be recalled or revoked by the directors at any time.

38. Audit
An auditor or auditors must be appointed and his or their duties regulated in accordance with the Act.

39. Execution of Deeds
39.1 The club shall not have a common seal.
39.2 The club may execute any deed by the authority of a resolution of the directors and in the presence of:
39.2.1 at least two directors and
39.2.2 the secretary or another person appointed by the directors for the purpose.
39.3 The two directors and the secretary or the other person appointed must sign every instrument in the presence of each other.

40. Dissolution
If the club is wound up, whether voluntarily or otherwise, the liquidator may, with the sanction of an extraordinary resolution of the club and any other sanction
required by the Act:
40.1 divide among the members in specie or in kind, the whole or any part of the assets of the club and
40.2 vest the whole or any part of the assets of the club in trustees upon such trusts
for the benefit of the members as he, with the same sanction, determines.

41. Notices
41.1 A notice may be given by the club to any member personally, by sending it by post in a prepaid envelope addressed to the member at his registered address
or by posting it in a conspicuous place in the clubhouse of the club.
41.2 Where a notice is sent by post, service of the notice is deemed to be effected by properly addressing, prepaying and posting a letter containing the notice and
is deemed to have been effected at the expiration of 48 hours after the envelope containing it was posted.

42. Headings
The headings in these articles do not form part of them or in any manner affect the interpretation or construction of them.

Club Notes

Commodore

I can only apologise to members for the conditions at the Club as a result of the rewiring of the Cruiser Park.. When
we decided to go ahead with the project after the delay caused by our acquiring the site, we were initially told that
the contractor would dig the trenches, lay the cables and backfill the trenches in three weeks. As you are aware this
has taken much longer but once started, we were rather stuck with finishing.

Looking forward we have the Laying Up Supper on 8" November and the Annual General Meeting on 23"
November. Immediately prior to the Annual General Meeting, we are holding the last AGM of the Marconi Sailing
Section of the MASC. This meeting will receive the final account and vote on the dissolution of the section.
One of the items to be resolved at the AGM is the name of the club for the future. I would like to thank Clive
Shenton for organising the straw poll to establish the names that will be put to the vote. These are in alphabetical
order:

Marconi Sailing Club
Stansgate Abbey Sailing Club
Thirslet Sailing Club

About the only downside that has come to our notice of buying the site from MASC, is that we are now being
charged for the use of rooms at Beehive Lane. In order to keep the cost down we are holding the Executive
meetings in our houses and the Management Committee meeting in the village hall at East Hanningfield. The other
subcommittees are also making alternative arrangements.
Partly for this reason and because of the reduced attendance last year, Roger Camp is holding the
Cruiser Fleet AGM at the club and may not have any winter lectures.
However I have received an invitation from the Royal Harwich Yacht Club and details of their lecture programme
(printed elsewhere in this edition of Navigans). If you are interested in attending, contact their secretary direct:
Colin Burrows Tel [redacted]19 or email secretary@rhy.demon.co.uk. In addition to the lecture, they can provide
an excellent supper before the talk for £8.00 per head, again contact the secretary direct no later than the Monday
before the talk.

I look forward to seeing you all at the AGM on 23 November.

Neil Pembleton

Handicap Fleet

End of season wash-up
Here we are at the end of the season and it seems like months since I remembered to get an article to Matt in time
for the deadline! Whilst I haven’t been afloat quite so much as I might have liked, the fleet has had a varied and
interesting season, with a pleasing number of competitors in Sunday (and Wednesday night) racing throughout the
season. I don’t mean by this to exclude our Saturday sailors, or those who like to creek crawl, cruise or just practise
turning their boats upside down then the right way up again (my own favoured past-time) — racing is simply the
more visible side of handicap fleet sailing at our club. It has been particularly pleasing to see new members joining
and sailing regularly as part of the fleet, as well as the many new boats that have arrived and added to the variety of
handicap boats.

Dinghy Park
One of the most obvious developments in the fleet during the season is certainly the change to the layout to the
dinghy park. An obvious improvement, after early teething problems, was the increased widths of the gangways in
the dinghy park, making rigging and de-rigging easier than in previous years. It also made use of the additional
space afforded to us by the slight extension to the south of the park. I am aware, however, that as the season
progressed, new members, and others bringing boats to the club later in the season, experienced difficulties in

2

a
finding spaces for boats, and we had to resort to filling in gaps at the ends of rows. We will be looking at the layout
again this winter to try and alleviate the problem for next year. If you have any comments or thoughts that may help
us in this process, do contact me (details below) or Barry Hutt, Dinghy Park Secretary.

Trailer Sailers
Developing on the above theme, one area which I am keen to understand better is that of trailer sailers. These have,
traditionally, been stored in the dinghy park during the summer, but the growing demand for spaces in the dinghy
park has made this harder this year. It has been suggested that the best solution to this may be to dedicate an area in
the catamaran park to trailer sailers - these spaces could be available both for summer and winter storage. Could
members who consider their boat to be a day or trailer sailer (the definition is a little hazy within the club) please
contact Roger Camp, Cruiser Fleet Captain on [redacted] or [redacted].co.uk. Roger will be able to
advise you on a suitable location for your boat that will allow it sufficient space and car access for when you want

CADET WEEK 2003

During the preparations for “Cadet Week 2003” we started to look for an interesting logo for the T-shirts. Last year we had 50 years of sailing at Marconi Sailing Club so we thought it might be a significant anniversary for the Cadet fleet. We talked to several likely members in an attempt to establish a history of the early days but with not much luck until Maureen Ball, who spent a lot of time trawling through Navigans, came up with following;

Birth of the Cadet Fleet in the Marconi Sailing Club - at Heybridge

Before the days of the Cadet Fleet: In October 1957 a series of winter classes was proposed to teach the adult novices the theory of sailing. In the February/March 1961 Navigans there were proposals to consider creating a Junior Membership of the Club for youngsters aged 16-21.

1961 - The Cadet Fleet came into being at the Club's AGM on Thursday 30th November 1961 when 'R.F.S.'
(Robbie Sims) reported on "the keen way in which the younger members of the Club have banded together to form a Cadet group and elected John Littlewood as their Cadet Captain designate. In the light of such enthusiasm the Club can do little else but make them an official branch of the sailing club."

1962 - Four Cadet Races were held during the 1962 sailing season; on 2nd June, 1st July, 2nd September, and the
4th race perhaps in early October (before publication of October Navigans). It was to be an irregular series of races
for cadets aged under 18 who could sail either their own boats or boats borrowed from other members.

In November 1962:
The Payne Trophy (for Cadet Racing) was won by J. Bigden.
The Fred Garrett Memorial Trophy was awarded to John Hutchings - presumably then as now, the trophy
was awarded to the most outstanding cadet member of the year for reasons other than racing.

1963 - The Club began its move from Heybridge to Stansgate in the Spring of 1963.

In the 1963 sailing season just two dates were mentioned for cadet races - 20th July and 21st September. In August
a party of Marconi SC Cadets, with three Fleetwinds and a Graduate, were the guests of the Maylandsea Bay Yacht Club for their cadet week during August. Four days of handicap races and a variety of other events including a film show and a party for evening entertainment, followed by transport to Maldon for the Carnival Week fireworks. A party of cadets also visited the Blackwater SC for their cadet week and were guests at an evening party at the Blackwater Clubhouse.

In November 1963: Payne Trophy won by Ian Shaw
Fred Garrett Memorial Trophy awarded to Michael Eyre.

1964 - On 4th April a Cadet Party was held - ticket price 2/6d. Cadet Races were held on 18th April, 2nd May,
14th June, 20th June, 15th August, Cadet Open on 22-23 August. Cadets warmly thanked for all the help
they gave at the Fleetwind Nationals with shore based help, manning rescue boats, providing refreshments and helping to clear up after the party.

By July 1964: The small sailing boat "Brazil" had been given by Mrs Sutherland to the Club who planned to make it available particularly for the younger sailors. It was a glassfibre Solent Scow 11'3" long and rigged with a single terylene lugsail. It was much welcomed by the Club who had had to sell the Club's sailing boat 'Avril' late in 1963 because the cost in cash or volunteer time to restore her to useable condition was too great -'a casualty of the move to Stansgate.'

Note that in July 1964 Navigans, just as today, members were being warned that venomous snakes may be infesting the sea wall and grassland area by the gun emplacement at Stansgate. Navigans stated that "should a bite occur, the nearest doctor holding snake bite serum is Dr Warren at Southminster, failing this, Chelmsford

6
hospital." Some grass clearance had been attempted but the grass is the responsibility of the River Board
and as it was binding the banks of the sea wall it was grown there for a specific reason.

In November 1964: Payne Trophy won by S. Darney
Fred Garrett Memorial Trophy awarded to John Hutchings.

There were now 46 Cadet members in the Club among the total of 513 subscription-paying members consisting of
Marconi Employees/Family members; Associate (non-Marconi) Members/Family members, and Cadets.

(Peter continues)
This revealed that it was 42 years since the formation of the Cadet Fleet, not a traditional anniversary, but it
identified John Littlewood as our first fleet captain. It also set us thinking that it would be nice to have a permanent
record of past fleet captains. So what seemed to be a good idea would be to have a perpetual trophy for each new
fleet captain to hold for the year. To this end we bought a shield and had it engraved with James Tovey as the first
recipient. He then presented it to Sophie Hurrell-Smith. What we would like to do is to engrave a plate on the back
with all previous fleet captains. So please own up! Contact me, Pete Clayton on [redacted] if you are a past
fleet captain or know some one who was.

John and Sue Littlewood kindly agreed to present the prizes at the end of Cadet Week this year. John made a short
speech to open the prize giving, the notes from which I have included, with his permission, as they give an
interesting insight into the beginnings of the Cadet Fleet.

John’s notes

When I was 13 my dad and I built a canoe in the dining room, much to my mother’s delight, which whilst half
finished was kept in my bedroom.

With school I went on an expedition to paddle from Maldon to Harwich. We reached as far as Clacton, sleeping
over night at St Osyth on the beach. This was my first experience on the river.

Two years later when I was 15 I joined the Marconi Sailing club at Heybridge with Roger Smith who now sails in
the Solo fleet.

The club was on a barge, the Mamgu, which had reached the end of her sailing career and was permanently
moored.

The Mamgu was rather a special barge, built as a yacht with a counter stern and lots of heavy wood panelling,
bathrooms and a stone floored galley and needed a lot of maintenance.

The club moorings dried out at low water and were spread around the Mamgu.

Most weekends during the summer Roger and I would travel to Maldon on the train and walk down the canal to
Heybridge.

There were around 10 cadets who would arrive on a Friday evening or Saturday morning and stay until late
afternoon on Sunday.

We used to lark about a lot and spend most of the night shuffling around Heybridge basin after our half of cider in
the Jolly Sailor until we could stay awake no longer. We would then sleep on the saloon floor.

One night we had watched someone a little worse for wear try to drive his car into the canal, saved only by the
mooring lines of a suitable positioned boat.

For food we ate mostly chocolate, crisps from the galley, baked beans, bread brought from home and the rare
delicacy introduced by one of our group, “Rice Pudding and Jam Sandwiches”.

We would crew for members in the racing, operate the rescue launch, borrow other members boats and hire the
club boat — an old Gunter rigged half Decker called Avril.

Like now, once a year most of the regular club members would sail to Osea for a day on the beach and the annual
“Mud fight” just behind the shingle spit.

Also, for several years we begged, borrowed or stole boats and sailed down the river for a weeks Dingy camping
with a cover over the boom and wet sleeping bags.

By what I have seen, we did not have the skills you have or the training you receive during cadet week.

Most of my experience was gained crewing for Terry Hallam (you can see his name on the past Commodores
board). He had an old Ramsgate smack converted with a Bermudan rig and a cabin. This had very leaky garboards
that means we were very familiar with the bilge pump, especially when going to windward.

We went to Mersea, Wivenhoe, Brightlingsea, Pin Mill, Burnham and the river Roach and I was very lucky to learn
a lot about boats and the Essex coast.

When I was 17 we started the move to Stansgate. This meant we had to get motorbikes but we were still able to
camp at the weekends. We did have to change our Pub to the “Sun and Anchor”.

These fields were empty and old Farmer Sparrow kept a bull where we park our cars today. It did have a fence but
was still treated with a lot of respect.

Where the concrete base stands we built the first club hut. This project was managed by an engineer called Alan
Pratt. I can remember it being christened by Jack Bigden, I believe “The house that Pratt built”.

Alan was a fine engineer and mathematician. I later spent my first East Anglian Cruiser races, the Sunk race and
Ostend race, amongst others, in a boat in which he was Navigator. We never got lost.

I say this was the second building on site — the portaloo was the first. This was sited just to the west of the
floodgates. If you were smart you would make sure you did not need to use it when it was full. You would find
yourself carrying it to the river to empty first.

When i started sailing, fibreglass and the Mirror dinghy were not invented. The boats we had were mostly
plywood, Heron, Fleetwing, Enterprise, Osprey, Albacore, Flying Dutchman and a little later the Hornet and
Fireball.

We also used a number of older boats like the Blackwater one design and the International Sharpie, which are still
sailed at Wells-Next-The-Sea in Norfolk.

I hope you have enjoyed the week and will keep up sailing as long as I have. It has been a hobby which has held
my interest all my life and which I have shared with my family, my friends and their friends.

I think the best weeks in the year at the Club are camping and Cadet week.

Long may it continue.

Pete Clayton

What’s in a name?

With regard to your task of seeking members views of what our sailing club should be called. I would like to make
the following comments.

MARCONI SAILING CLUB

Being a traditionalist I am in favour of retaining “MARCONI SAILING CLUB” for the following reasons;

1) The Club has recently celebrated its 50" anniversary and has a lot to be proud of, in particular the goof it
has done for both “RYA Sailability” and “Cirdan Trust”. Regarding the former, “Marconi Challenger” can
still be seen sailing at Grafham water plus of course there are other Marconi Challengers elsewhere giving
pleasure to disabled sailors.
2) “MARCONI SAILING CLUB” is known throughout not only for its ability to host open events but also for
the quality of its helms.
3) The Cruiser Fleet has taken the clubs burgee far and wide and can be seen in many clubs and ports of call
where the name MARCONI is instantly recognised and respected.
4) If it were not for the dedication and foresight of our founder members, we would not have a sailing club at
all.
5) As for the general public thinking you have to be a Marconi employee before being able to join. I would
point out that over the past few years out non Marconi membership ratio has been far greater. It is up to us
to make the public aware.
6) Let us not get carried away by the mismanagement of two so called financial directors, let us instead
remember the technical achievements created under the name MARCONI and be proud of that association.
7) Lastly, I would point out Maldon District Council through the River Bailiff installed and charted a
navigation mark off the clubhouse called “Marconi”.

STANSGATE SAILING CLUB or STANSGATE ABBEY SAILING CLUB

If we have to change the name then I favour either one of these titles. It states where we are, the name is at the top
of the road leading down to the club and of course it recognises the connection with our President Tony Benn.

THIRSLET SAILING CLUB

I fail to see any connection with this name and our sailing club. Thirslet is a piece of land some two miles east of
the club which shows itself only at low water and is an inconvenience to sailing although I suppose its fine for
picnics.

Ladder Safety

A recent accident at club is a timely reminder to all cruiser owners to check the state of their favourite ladder. Often
the ladder that is used for the boat is a cast off from home, it’s not safe to use for painting the house but it is safe for
climbing on and off the boat in the cruiser park. The rungs of wooden ladders rot quickly when left in the open and
it may not be obvious that they have reached their sell be date, until too late. An Aluminium ladder is a better
alternative and even then it needs to be tied securely to the boat.

In the recent incident, a ladder accident caused a head injury serious enough to warrant the air ambulance being
called and landing on the hard to take the casualty to If only for the sake of the tenders that it cast adrift into
the Blackwater, let’s try and make it the last time.

2003 Helm of the Year Series

The Series this year took place on Saturday Sept 27, and was once again sailed in Bytes kindly loaned for the day
by members.

The Champions from 5 fleets took part, these being Roger Smith (Solo), Les Hurrell-Smith (Handicap), Jenny Ball
(Medium Cat), Tim Wallace (Fast Cat), and Nick Miller (Cadet).

The familiar format of 5 short races, where contestants sail a different boat in each race, was followed. Committee
boat starts were used to provide a windward first leg of the course.

Race 1 was set with a beat across the tide to No.1 mark, but unfortunately the force 2 wind faded just after the start,
making progress against wind and tide tortuously slow. Nick made a very prudent long port tack up the tide from
the start and this enabled him to establish a big lead at the windward mark, followed by Jenny, Tim, Les, and
Roger. This remained the order at the end of the lap, but during the slow beat in lap 2 both Tim and Les managed to
wriggle past Jenny to claim 2TM and 3TM spots. Jenny finished 4" in front of Roger. This race had taken significantly
longer than the R.O. intended, due to the failing wind, and with no sign of freshening it was decided to take an
early lunch.

After lunch the wind had moved easterly but was not much stronger, so a different course was set in-shore in the
bay near Ramsey Island. This provided protection from the tide and good viewing on the bank for the spectators.

In Race 2 Nick again was quickest off the line and established a good lead at the windward mark from Jenny and
Tim, with Roger and Les following at a respectful distance. Tim dived past Jenny on the first run to snatch a 2TM
place that he held to the finish, with Nick again showing his rivals the way home.

Race 3 saw Nick in charge once again, leading the others round the windward mark in the order, Jenny, Tim, Les,
and Roger. The latter two were battling hard with Roger taking 4" on the second beat which he narrowly held to the
finish.

Nick was again in front early in Race 4, but Roger was clearly beginning to get the hang of the Byte as he led the
others round the windward mark with Jenny in front of Tim and Les. The latter three were very closely matched on
the reaches in what was the most competitive race yet, but Tim showed some good downwind speed to pass Jenny
and Roger. Nick sailed serenely on to record another victory.

Nick and Roger both sailed good first beats in the final race with Roger closing on Nick’s transom on the
subsequent run in the only real challenge to Nick’s domination of the series. However, Nick soon opened a gap on
the second lap and Tim and Jenny both closed up on Roger, passing him on the final beat. Nick received a warm
round of applause as he crossed the finish line having deservedly claimed the title “Helm of the Year”.

Club Notes

Commodore

As you are aware this is the last time that I will be writing Commodores notes following my late decision to stand
down this year for personal reasons. I am extremely pleased that Chris Davies has agreed to being nominated to
succeed myself and wish him well in the post.

The company formed to acquire the site requires that there are six "Directors" for legal reasons who form the
Executive Committee. These are the Commodore, two Vice Commodores, two Rear Commodores and the
Honorary Treasurer. Again you will be aware from the Annual General Meeting notice that Peter Clayton, Ray
Ball, Clive Shenton, Claire Davies and John Bird will be filling these roles.
I believe that this team, along with Pat Black as Company Secretary, offers a brilliant blend of experience,
innovation and youth to lead the Club into the next phase of its development, independent of the MASC.

The By Laws of the Club were published in last month's Navigans and included the new Sub Committee structure
which we believe recognises the functions of the Club and new responsibilities placed on us as a company. I am
pleased to see that people have come forward to fill the main positions on these Sub Committees and again that we
have an excellent mix of experience and new talent.
They, along with the Executive, form the Management Committee to take the Club forward into the future.
Retaining the principles of the founder members whilst recognising the different requirements of today, both in
relation to leisure time and legislation.

This year has seen tremendous strides by the Club but I have been saddened by a number of incidents during the
year;

Traditionally the shingle strip between the hard and the scrubbing posts has been left clear by the dinghy fleets for
use by tenders from the cruisers etc. On a number of occasions this year the area has been completely blocked
during the lunch break by dinghies on trolleys. On at least one occasion this was largely caused by those returning
first from racing not pulling their trolleys far enough up the hard to allow others to come onto it.

On the last Saturday of the camping fortnight there had obviously been a party in the Dell Bar. On the Sunday
morning it was left to Mike Smith and Chris Pitak to clean up the mess left in there. It would have been nice if
some of those who had been involved on the Saturday night had done this.

Again at some time during the same fortnight, a dinghy was dragged across the garden by the patio. Probably
because of other boats blocking the way. Bob and Elsie Anderson were considerably upset by this after the hard
work that they put in. The situation was not helped by a thoughtless comment made to them "What else do you
expect, this is a sailing club". Yes, we are a sailing club but many unnamed individual members of the club put a
lot of time and effort into providing the well equipped, smart and tidy club in which we all can take pride. Let's not
destroy this aspect of the club through a few thoughtless actions.

I feel privileged to have been able to serve the Club in the last two years but I could not have achieved the purchase
of the site without the support of the other members of the Executive and Management Committee and most of all
the whole hearted support of all of you, its members.

I wish the Club and its members, all the best for the future.

Neil Pembleton

Some Notes on the Club Security System. (Gate Cards)

Our club members have the unusual privilege of access to the site and clubhouse at any time they wish. This is
achieved by means of access cards, which have a magnetic strip that may be programmed. Some cards provide
access to the first floor bar and the cellar. Access to these will depend on the responsibilities of the member. Each
card has a serial number associated with the member so that each card is unique. If a member leaves the club the
card will be cancelled so that it will no longer provide access. Every time a card is used the reader consults a list
to see if the card holder has the right of access. Ordinary cards are normally issued by the Club Registrar.
(Membership Secretary).

Occasionally a member will lose ‘their’ card and will then seek a replacement. After a new card is issued the
original card is cancelled. If the member subsequently rediscovers ‘their’ lost card it will be useless and should be
returned to the club. The cards have nothing visibly written on them except for the serial number. There is nothing
to associate the card with the sailing club so that our security is not significantly jeopardised in the interval before
the card is cancelled.

It is inevitable that other members when they have forgotten to bring ‘their’ own card or when they have
temporarily mislaid it will borrow a card from another member. If you borrow a card it is essential to return the
card you borrowed and not the mislaid card. If you subsequently leave the club ‘your’ card will be cancelled. If
this has earlier been swapped with another members card, that member will be denied access to the club.
Unfortunately the serial numbers on the cards wear off with time. This makes the recognition of swapped cards
impossible without a card reader. In the future the serial number will be marked on the card using a more
permanent method.

There are times when the card readers fail. The degradation is usually due to wear and is progressive resulting in
some cards being recognised whilst others are rejected. In this situation we endeavour to repair the card reader as
soon as possible. We can only apologise to those members who have been inconvenienced.

Misalignment of the gate or door is another recurring fault. The relative position of the mechanism is critical and
changes in temperature and humidity can cause misalignment. Rough usage will also cause misalignment.

Frank Bennett created the security system some 10 years ago and for a large proportion of the time it performs
satisfactorily. The alternative was to purchase a proprietary system with a maintenance contract at considerable
expense to the club.

We hope you find these notes helpful in explaining the background to the operation of the security system together
with some of its limitations. Perhaps it is worth making the following points.

1. Treat ‘your’ card with the same respect as your bank card. Keep it clear of magnets.(Car radio speakers).
2. Operate the gate to the site and the door to the clubhouse with care.

3. Ensure that you keep the card that was issued to you and make a note of the serial number. This is
particularly important if you have more than one card.

4. Ifyou are likely to be leaving the site when few other members are around use ‘your’ own card to check its
operation. Don’t just follow another member in.

5. If ‘your’ card is worn or damaged please ask for a replacement.

6. All cards remain the property of the Club.

Frank Bennett and David Steward

Commodore’s Comments

It is with some surprise that | find myself writing this piece. My expectation, like yours, was that Neil would carry on in post
for some time yet. He was very much the right Commodore at the right time; he steered us magnificently through the minefield
that was the purchase of the Club and we all owe him a debt of gratitude.

The Executive team has seen some changes of personnel and is enlarged; we now have two Vice Commodores and two Rear
Commodores. This increase was designed to enable us to better deal with the additional administrative and management loads
placed on us as a result of our new-found independence.

| am delighted that Pat Black and John Bird have agreed to stay on as Secretary and Treasurer respectively. The two Vice
Commodores are Ray Ball and Peter Clayton; Claire Davies and Clive Shenton take on the two Rear Commodore roles. Ray
will major on matters concerning the Clubhouse and site; Peter will take responsibility for issues concerning equipment and
moorings, camping and Cadet training; Claire will look after all sailing matters and Clive takes over responsibility for ECPR and
social activities. | think this makes a very strong team; | am grateful for their support and confident that in turn they will get full
support from Club members.

| won’t name the Management Committee individually here. Their names will appear in the new Handbook and the roles they
take on are broadly understood. They contribute significantly to the smooth running of the club; their commitment is widely
appreciated.

| do not overlook the efforts of a much larger band of members who, working within the Club's self-help ethos, do so much -
sometimes on a regular basis, sometimes on an occasional basis - to assist with the running of the Club. This involvement is a
major contributor to the character of the Club. We all go through periods where work, family or personal circumstances prevent
us from being as involved as we might wish - but all contributions are welcome, no matter how small or irregular. Management
Committee provides the focus for that effort - to discuss doing more or any ideas, make contact with someone on that list.

Now a few words about our intended focus for the coming year. Recent concern has been for the purchase of the site and the
creation of a financial plan to support that activity - with some valuable work being done to maintain the site. Now we need to
carefully take stock of what we have bought and how we use it, so that we have the information to develop from our strong
financial plan. However, this does not imply a period of introspection and no activity - there is a lot to be done to ensure that the
site is maintained in safe, practical and presentable order. There is also a case for reviewing the most important aspect of our
existence as a Club - our sailing!.

So three initiatives are born:
e Knowledge Fund will pull together all the information we can gather about the site, site facilities and how members
use the site and all it contains. This information will aid our decisions in managing and developing the site.
e _ Foresail will re-examine all sailing activity with a view to identifying anything that we could do better or more often and
to consider new ways in which we might improve what we offer to members and potential members.
e Homepride will address the need to maintain the site in good order and to present the Club facilities in such a way
that they are pleasing to existing members and attractive to potential members.

Everyone will have an opportunity to be involved. A lot of the information-gathering will be done through the Fleet structure. So
please be prepared to be involved in a series of activities that are important to our future as an independent club.

| hope you all had a Happy Christmas; have an Excellent New Year!

Chris Davies

Retiring Commodore - A few final notes

Many thanks to all who attended the Annual General Meeting and contributed to the discussion.

As you will be aware the vote to select a new name for the Club resulted in the decision to retain the name "Marconi Sailing
Club". This was selected by an overall majority over the other two names which had emerged as "front runners". Subject to
Chris Davies and the new executive establishing that there is no legal problem, this will be the name.

One of the duties of the Commodore each year is to decide who will receive three of the Club Trophies.
Firstly there is the Mamgu which is awarded for the best log submitted by 1*' October each year. | received two entries and the
award went to Les Hurrell-Smith for his log entitled "Three men and a boat - the tale of a yacht delivery" which | found
informative, amusing and educational.

The next is the Seamanship Trophy which is awarded to a person who has performed an act of outstanding seamanship. Again
there were two entries and it went to Nick Miller and Rob Mead jointly following the dismasting of Rob's Pico and the retrieval of
him and his dinghy by Nick in another Pico. Although this happened locally to the Club during Camping fortnight when the safety
boats were available, both of them dealt with the situation using their own resources and skills rather than assuming that Rob
would be "rescued". It is also appropriate to associate the work of the Cadet Tutors with this event as they instilled the ethos of
self reliance into the cadet fleet

Minutes of MSC Cruiser Fleet AGM 22TM Nov 2003

Apologies were received from Pat Black, Derek Kirby, Gordon Pewter, Julie Bloomfield Mick and Roger, Derek and Hilary
Gardiner and Malcolm and Helen Shaft.

Review of 2003 Sailing Season
There were three winter meetings including a talk from the Port of London Authority, ICOM and a quiz.

In May fifty six people attended the fitting out supper and eighteen boats went to Burnham. In June thirteen boats visited
Brightlingsea and the Watercress Run on the 19th June was well attended with about nineteen boats and fifty people attending
the evening barbeque. The ECPR was less well supported than usual this year and it would be nice to have more volunteers
next year. Chris Davies announced that a sum in excess of £9,000 had been donated from the ECPR to the Cirdan Trust and
thanked the cruiser fleet for their support. Nineteen boats locked into St Katherine’s Dock for the start of the summer cruise with
fifteen going onto to Chatham where there was another successful barbeque. Fewer people than normal made it to Shotley this
year with about sixteen boats locking in and only sixteen attending the Sunday dinner.

Review of 2003 Racing Season
Five races were held; the Doctor was run in conjunction with BJRC, the Eagle trophy was run from the club to Burnham, while
the Medusa finished by joining the rest of the club in Brightlingsea. The Steeple Bay trophy was new in joining catamarans and
dinghies from the club, and the Knoll trophy was a new and successful single handed event. The diary for next year is still to be
decided but will comprise five races maintaining the Jackpot and the single handed. There is also a possibility of a pursuit race.

Winter Storage and Cruiser Haul Out
Electrics. Roger asked Dave Payne to explain the electrical re-fit in the cruiser park. Dave Payne outlined the reasons for the
refit due to non compliance of current regulations. The new system will ensure ample to supply to the far end of the cruiser park
and that no one will be able to leave multiple electrical appliances plugged in for long periods. Six amp breakers have been
installed on outlets with a welding socket on the cruiser garage, and on the winch hut.

Bob Godbold was reassured that pressure washers would be able to be used in the cruiser park and Pete Bloomfield was
assured that breakers in the engine shed would not trip. Mark queried why new bollards only had two outlets but Dave pointed
out that outlets been over doubled. Mike Smith was told that if an appliance cut out there was a button on the outlet post to
reset the club RCD. There followed discussion over the concern that boats that have their own electrical supply could cause, if
live and neutral are transposed, their trailers to give off electric shocks. It was suggested that, until there had been further
discussion at committee which would result in recommendations in Navigans, no one plug their electrical circuit into the club
supply but use a wander lead instead. No plugs are to be left plugged into the main supply unless the owner is on Site. Plugs
are available from Dave at a cost of £2.00

Tractors and Haul Out
Murray was pleased that the season had started and finished with four working tractors. The club is looking to replace the four
wheel drive tractor in the near future. (Since the AGM, the hydraulic winch engine has failed and is to be replaced with an
electric motor.) Roger thanked Murray and this was endorsed by members.

Moorings
Peter Clayton mooted several options to cut down workload on mooring laying and lifting. These were discussed but a majority
voted for the continuation of the present system for reliability reasons. There was a discussion about the logistics of the make
up of mooring teams as some had been found to be excessively onerous. This will be investigated. Murray urged people to
inspect their moorings during the winter and not to wait until inspection day. There was a discussion about the need to weld
shackles.

Chain
Don Holdsworth has shackles for sale at £3.00 for % and £2.00 for 5/8. He urged people to change to heavier chain for their
risers which he has available at a cost of £1.75 per foot for 14 mm.

Paint
Gordon Preston will sell paint and stated that prices will be more or less maintained. Details will go in Navigans as usual.
Delivery will probably be a week later.

Programme 2004
There will be no winter meetings due to the expense of hiring the Chelmsford MASC rooms. There is a possibility of a bowling
evening in February and there will need to be a spring meeting at the club. The fitting out supper is booked for 8" May and the
season will continue as follows:

Burnham on 29/30/31" May with a meal in the Swallowtail on the Sunday.
Heybridge on 19" June.
Brightlingsea on 3/4" July.
ECPR 24'/25" July. There is a need for more cruisers.
Ramsgate, Dover, Chatham week beginning 31° July
August Bank Holiday with Shotley as a start. No restaurant is being booked this year so it was suggested that people book up
the Shipwreck for themselves.

Cock Up Trophy
There were several contenders but, as is traditional, only those who attended the meeting know the results.

Any Other Business
Neil Pembleton thanked Frank Burgess and Roger Camp for their efforts.

Roger closed the meeting at 4.45
